questions.prompt: In the tea + sugar test, what is the dependent variable (what you measure)?

choices.text: Amount of sugar
How sweet it tastes
Stir time
Cup size

questions.explanation: DV = sweetness (measured). IV = sugar amount. Controls include stir time, tea type, temperature.
questions.science_idea: Name IV, DV, and controls for every investigation.

questions.prompt: More sugar → sweeter tea? You add more sugar and also stir longer each time. What's the problem?

choices.text: Unfair — sugar and stir time both changed
Fair — stirring helps you taste better
Unfair — tea should be cold
Fair — sweetness is easy to judge

questions.explanation: Keep stir time the same so sugar is the only change.

questions.prompt:
Text 'lab sketch':
  Cup1: 100 ml water, 1 sugar spoon, stir 10 s, taste
  Cup2: 100 ml water, 3 sugar spoons, stir 10 s, taste
  Cup3: 100 ml water, 5 sugar spoons, stir 30 s, taste
Which cup breaks the fair test, and how?

choices.text: Cup3 — stir time jumped to 30 s while sugar also changed
Cup1 — too little sugar
Cup2 — middle values are always wrong
All fair — water volume matched

questions.explanation: Cups 1–2 keep stir time fixed; Cup3 adds a second IV (stir time).
questions.science_idea: Scan a procedure like a diagram: find the row that breaks the pattern.

questions.prompt: Match the science word to its job in an investigation.

choices.text: IV=deliberate change; DV=measured outcome; Controls=kept constant; Confound=accidental extra change
IV=measured outcome; DV=deliberate change; Controls=accidental; Confound=kept constant
All four mean 'what you measure'
IV and DV are the same thing

pairs.right: The one factor you deliberately change
An accidental extra change that muddies results

questions.explanation: Stretch vocab: naming a confound shows you can critique a messy test.
